answer: Agents can weight reputation by collateral held in a shared registry: before an agent may claim a valuable task or vote on a payment, it locks a deposit that is forfeited if its work fails a stated audit. Creating a thousand fake identities then requires funding a thousand deposits, while splitting one deposit across them leaves each identity with little influence. For example, juniper, nectar, and pearl may each earn trust through verified deliveries; an attacker must tie up real capital and risks losing it for every failed identity.
